settings.text: A duvet filling lasts longest when the cover does most of the work. Wash the cover often and the filling rarely.
settings.note: General guidance. This is general advice for caring for cotton, cotton satin and polyester fills. It is not specific to one product. Always follow the care label on your item first.

settings.heading: Everyday care
settings.text:
• Always use a duvet cover. It keeps the filling clean and is much easier to wash.
  • Shake the duvet each morning to spread the filling evenly and keep its loft.
  • Air it now and then in fresh air, out of strong direct sun.

settings.heading: Washing the cover
settings.text:
• Wash duvet covers as you would your sheets: similar colours, mild detergent, a cool or warm wash.
  • Close buttons or zips first and turn the cover inside out.
  • Wash two-tone and strongly coloured covers on their own for the first few washes.

settings.heading: Cleaning the filling
settings.text:
• Spot-clean small marks on the shell with a damp cloth and a little mild detergent.
  • Only machine wash a filling if its care label allows it. A large duvet needs a large-capacity machine or a laundry service.
  • Rinse well. Detergent left in the fill can make it clump.

settings.heading: Drying
settings.text:
• Dry the filling completely before using or storing it. Damp filling can clump and smell musty.
  • If the label allows a dryer, use a low heat and stop now and then to shake the duvet out.
  • Otherwise dry it flat or over a wide rail, turning it often.

settings.heading: Storing in warm months
settings.text:
• Store the duvet clean and fully dry when the weather warms up.
  • Use a breathable cotton bag rather than plastic, in a cool, dry place.
  • Avoid keeping it tightly compressed for long periods. Shake it out well when you bring it back.

settings.question: How do I know a duvet filling needs replacing?
settings.answer: If it stays flat after a good shake, has lumps that will not spread out, or feels thin in places, it may be time for a new one.

settings.question: Can I wash a duvet filling at home?
settings.answer: Only if the care label allows it and it fits loosely in your machine. If in doubt, use a laundry service.
